messages:
Alyssa: quick heads-up — during the encryptops dry run I found ~0.6% of objects in s3://staging-archive missing SSE metadata. They still download but show up as unencrypted in our audit. cc @Mike @Jamal
Mike: can you paste the exact key(s) and the command you used?
Alyssa: ran:
```
aws s3api list-objects --bucket staging-archive --prefix backups/2026-03 | jq -r '.Contents[].Key' | xargs -I {} aws s3api head-object --bucket staging-archive --key {} --query '{Key:Key, SSE:ServerSideEncryption, Metadata:Metadata}'
```
example output:
```
{"Key":"backups/2026-03/tenant-42/dump.sql.gz","SSE":null,"Metadata":{}}
{"Key":"backups/2026-03/tenant-42/dump.sql.gz.part","SSE":"AES256","Metadata":{}}
```
Mike: hmm that null SSE looks bad — could be uploader skipping when it saw multipart temp file. @encops-bot any alerts about failed kms:Encrypt grants in last 48h?
SRE Bot: EncOps Alert: 2 failed PutObject operations (service=uploader, error=AccessDenied) — timestamps 2026-03-10T04:32Z, 2026-03-11T11:09Z. Trace: uploader-sa@project
Jamal: likely cause: uploader service account lost kms:Encrypt on the key due to a policy prune. Also multipart flows sometimes upload part with SSE unset. We should confirm IAM delta + check key's grant TTLs.
Sophia: also check key metadata: was there a scheduled rekey or HSM rotation? If grant TTL was short and long backups reused ephemeral grants, decrypt/encrypt could fail silently. run:
```
gcloud kms keys describe key-name --location global --keyring prod-kr --format json
# or aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/prod-enc
```
Mike: audit query I used to surface this earlier:
```
resource.type="gcs_bucket"
protoPayload.methodName="storage.objects.insert"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="uploader-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
logName="projects/REDACTED/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access"
```
filter by responseStatus.code = 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED) or look for missing ServerSideEncryption in write logs.
Alyssa: mitigation plan:
- run a one-off copy to enforce SSE-KMS for affected keys: `aws s3 cp s3://staging-archive/<key> s3://staging-archive/<key> --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/prod-enc`
- patch uploader to fail fast on HEAD object without SSE header and add a retry that requests a KMS grant
- add a periodic audit query + PagerDuty alert when unencrypted count > 0.1%
Mike: agree. Also add a bucket policy to require server-side encryption as a short-term enforcement: deny s3:PutObject when x-amz-server-side-encryption is absent.
Jamal: I'll open a tiny RBAC rollback ticket to re-add kms:Encrypt to uploader-sa and run a canary. tagging @Sophia for key policy review.
Sophia: will review key grants and confirm no rotation gaps. propose we run an incident drill and update the encryptops runbook with the audit queries and the copy-fix command.
Alyssa: thanks — I'll start a fix-run in a canary folder and report results here in ~30m :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
Mike: :thumbsup: 
Jamal: ping if you need help with the iam delta or quick grant patch.
